newsitem.title: CHINA: Sinopec '96 pre-tax profits down 2.2 bln yuan.
newsitem.headline: Sinopec '96 pre-tax profits down 2.2 bln yuan.

text.p: China National Petrochemical Corp, or Sinopec, posted pre-tax profits of 31.5 billion yuan ($3.8 billion) in 1996, down by 2.2 billion yuan from 1995, the Financial News said on Tuesday.
The newspaper did not give after-tax profits figures.

The state refiner faced tough market conditions in 1996, it said. China raised the average price of onshore crude oil by 68 yuan per tonne, prices of offshore oil were rising and those of imported crude oil surged.
Rising production costs in the petrochemical industry were also fuelled by soaring prices of coal, electricity and transport, the newspaper said.
Sinopec's sales were affected by weak domestic demand for chemicals and chemical fibres in 1996, it said, but gave no further details.
The company managed to cut production costs by more than 10 billion yuan in 1996 by adjusting its production structure and cutting back on expenses, it said.
